Quick findings from the telemetry side after a 10-min look:
- We have sustained queue growth on the request router for NovaMed's tenant id (queue depth up 6x from baseline).
- Backpressure is propagating into the KV cache causing higher miss rates (~18% -> 42%) which in turn increases per-token compute and exacerbates latency.
- Concurrency cap for that tenant was at our standard enterprise level; during a flurry of parallel batch exports we've hit a soft limit in the request multiplexor causing stalls.

Immediate mitigations I'm scheduling now (ETA 30-60m):
1) Apply a temporary per-tenant hard concurrency cap at 60% of current config (will shed new large batch jobs).
2) Enable request-shedding policy for background/bulk routes (drops/queues low-priority jobs).
3) Route batch export traffic to CPU fallback pool (best-effort) for 1 hour to clear backlog.

I estimate we can see p99 improvement within 30–45 minutes after the cap + shedding are applied; full backlog drain ~90 minutes depending on remaining queued work. We'll monitor KV cache churn; if miss rate remains high we'll consider a short cache flush on affected serving nodes (requires brief soft-handshake eviction window).

I'll post telemetry links and a short runbook after changes.

-marissa

Subject: FYI: NovaMed — throughput degen root-cause and immediate steps

Hannah / David — quick exec note on the NovaMed escalation: 

Summary: External customer NovaMed experienced significant long-tail latency and throughput drop tied to queue growth induced by concurrent large batch exports. Root cause appears to be multiplicative: tenant-level concurrency + KV cache thrash -> per-token compute increase -> queue propagation.

Immediate actions taken (completed):
- Applied temporary per-tenant hard concurrency cap (60% of normal)
- Enabled batch-route shedding for low-priority jobs
- Diverted background batch jobs to CPU fallback pool to drain backlog

Status: p99 improved ~65% within 35 minutes of mitigations; error rate reduced to baseline. Backlog still draining; full closure expected within 90–120 minutes from mitigation start. NovaMed agreed to temporary pause of non-essential exports.

Risks / follow-up:
- We should evaluate whether our default enterprise concurrency settings need traffic-pattern guarding (per-tenant burst protection).
- Consider automated KV cache throttling or eviction policy for high-miss tenants to prevent self-reinforcing thrash.
- Recommend post-mortem with NovaMed and PS to review billing window tolerances.

I'll schedule a short incident readout tomorrow and include telemetry snapshots.

Sean Gallagher
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
